completed_outcomes.outcome: Committed advisory-only correction and direct regression that proves attach -> start -> advance-with-why and digest continuity. Wave-2 repair then made the lane green on its own cache-clean full Linux suite without weakening what it proved: three stale #467 TripLedgerComplianceOnTheHardAdvisory expectations were realigned to the pending-gate wording and map/INDEX.md was regenerated. No test was deleted or weakened, and the shipped advisory wording was measured and found correct. WAVE-2 ENGINE: Wave-2 engine ruling executed: the human ruled the ENGINE must permit the start its HARD advisory instructs rather than the advisory being narrowed. _trip_hard_gate now records the one begin the advisory itself mandates (verb=start, target IS the active gate, gate is pending, keyed refresh-request on file) as `begin-instructed` instead of `begin-released`. The entry is still appended with the same nine fields, so nothing is hidden; it is simply not one of the two outcomes the compliance selectors count, so obeying the engine no longer renders as non-compliance. _trip_advisory's wording is byte-for-byte untouched. The compliance selectors needed no change. Five #467 tests were re-aimed onto genuinely self-chosen begins (reopen, and a start aimed at a gate the advisory never named) where their guarantee is untouched; none deleted, skipped or loosened. The deliberately-failing marker expectation is re-pinned to the pending wording the engine now makes true.

WAVE-2 ENGINE: 902dc940 (engine change). Red/green over engine behavior: new class TripInstructedBeginIsNotAnOffence fails 4/8 before and passes 8/8 after; falsifier independently reverted only checklist_engine.py and reproduced 3 failed/5 passed on the new class and 6 failed/444 passed on the whole engine file. Cache-clean full Linux suite 1 failed/2988 passed -> 0 failed/2997 passed, 7 skipped, 1129 subtests. Independent falsifier APPROVE with a 1152-state differential sweep: zero states differ in raise/entry-count/gate-status; exactly 3 states relabel.

wave_evidence.claim: The existing runtime path is legal and only its pending-HARD advice was misleading.
wave_evidence.expected: A focused advisory/test correction can prove the legal sequence without runtime changes.
wave_evidence.observed: 22 focused tests passed after a red assertion; reviewer found no runtime guard/default/verb/state/schema change.
wave_evidence.source: implementer attempt 2 and independent reviewer artifacts

wave_evidence.claim: The three failing #467 expectations were stale, not a sign the shipped pending-HARD wording is wrong.
wave_evidence.expected: If the tests predate the pending/in-progress distinction, their scenarios leave the active gate PENDING and the old prefix is simply the wrong branch's text.
wave_evidence.observed: All three scenarios leave the active gate pending, and the engine refuses `advance` on a pending gate ("g2 is 'pending', must be in-progress to advance"). The pre-change wording therefore named a command the engine rejects, which is the #510 defect itself. Realigning the prefixes turned the full suite green with the whole-string equality property intact.
wave_evidence.source: wave-2 repair commander, direct engine measurement plus cache-clean full-suite runs

wave_evidence.claim: The engine REFUSES the start its advisory instructs, so permitting it is the fix.
wave_evidence.expected: Obeying the advisory literally at a pending gate reached by the agent's own close is refused by _trip_hard_gate.
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED. Measured before changing anything: the advisory names an ORDER ('First request a refresh ...; then begin THIS guarded gate'). An agent following that order attaches the request first, which sends _trip_hard_gate down its RELEASE path — the start is PERMITTED and the gate opens. The predecessor's ('g3','begin-refused') came from starting BEFORE attaching, out of the advisory's stated order. The defect that fires on perfect obedience is the BRANDING, not a refusal.
wave_evidence.source: commander pre-change repro at the dispatch chokepoint, wave-2 engine

wave_evidence.claim: The refusal/ledger semantics are load-bearing, so the ruled fix may be structurally blocked (honest-null clause).
wave_evidence.expected: If #467's compliance semantics depend on the branded outcome, permitting/de-branding breaks work others depend on.
wave_evidence.observed: NOT a null, but the collision was real and confined. #467's central demonstration case WAS the engine-instructed case: four of its tests demonstrate `begin-released` using start at a pending active gate with a request on file — exactly what #510's advisory later began instructing. Resolution keeps #467's stated purpose ('what an agent over the line must not do is BEGIN work it cannot finish') and re-aims those tests onto begins that are genuinely the agent's own choice. A 1152-state differential sweep found the change relabels 3 states and widens nothing.
wave_evidence.source: pre-ruling 3 enumeration (whole-worktree sweep) + independent falsifier sweeps
